sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL  ON THE 9 TH OF JULY 2025
CRIMINAL
APPEAL No. 407 of 2004  RATAN LAL
Versus  THE STATE OF M.P.

Appearance:
 Shri S.B.Shrivastava- Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri S P Chadar- GA for the respondent/State.
 ORDER

This appeal has been filed on behalf of the appellant under Section 374 (2) of CRPC against the judgment dated 17.2.2004 passed by Special Judge, Seoni in Special Criminal Case No.24/2003,
whereby appellant has been convicted under Section 3 (1) (xii) of SC/ST (PA) Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 2 years with fine of Rs.10,000/-, with default stipulation.
2.

Prosecution story in brief is that appellant/accused repeatedly established physical relations with the prosecutrix against her will and without her consent and on the pretext that he will keep her as his wife but later on, appellant refused to keep the prosecutrix as his wife.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned trial Court has acquitted the appellant for the offence under Section 376 of IPC and Section 3(2) (v) of SC/ST (PA) Act but it has convicted and sentenced appellant under Section 3 (1) (xii) of SC/ST (PA) Act.

It is also urged that in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30820 2 CRA-407-2004 the instant case, Ex.P/1's Caste Certificate has been issued by Tahsildar, Seoni who is not competent to issue aforesaid caste certificate.
On above grounds, it has been prayed that learned trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.

Hence, appeal filed by the appellant be allowed and he be acquitted of the offence under Section 3 (1) (xii) of SC/ST (PA) Act.
4.
Learned Government Advocate for the State submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case, appellant cannot be sentenced with the period already undergone.

He further submits that trial Ratan Lal vs The State Of M.P. on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16533505/
1

sentences.text: Court has rightly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
No interference is required in the same and appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.

5. Heard and perused record of the case.
Analysis and Findings:-
6.

So far as appellant's conviction under Section 3 (1) (xii) of SC/ST (PA) Act is concerned, one of the primary/basic/fundamental requirement of law is that prosecution is required to establish that complainant/victim belongs to/is member of scheduled caste & prosecution must prove this fact by production of caste certificate purported to have been issued by competent authority.

As per Government of Madhya Pradesh, General Administration Department Notification No.
F.7-2/96/Reservation Cell/one, Dated 1.8.96 (w.e.f.1 August 1996) only Collector/Additional District Collector/Deputy Collector/Sub-Divisional Officer is competent/authorized to issue permanent caste certificate.

In this court's opinion, above fact can not be proved by oral testimony/admissions made in examination u/s 313 of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:30820 3 CRA-407-2004 CrPC or by production of certificate issued by any authority other than Sub- Divisional Officer.
7.
Perusal of impugned judgment reveals that prosecution has not filed/produced any such caste certificate, purported to have been issued by competent authority as above.

It is also evident from impugned judgment that learned trial court has, just on the basis of Ex.P/1's caste certificate issued by Tahsildar has concluded/held that it is established that complainant/victim belongs to/is member of scheduled caste.
In this court's considered opinion, this finding of learned trial court is erroneous & against law.
Hence, in the instant case, it is not established that complainant/victim is member of Schedule Caste.

8. Further, evidently, learned trial Court has acquitted appellant for the offence under Section 376 of IPC but it has convicted and sentenced the appellant on the same set of evidence for the offence under Section 3(1) (xii) of SC/ST (PA) Act
. In this Court's considered opinion, as learned trial Court has acquitted the appellant for the offence under Section 376 of IPC.

Therefore, learned trial Court was not justified in convicting and sentencing the appellant for the offence under Section 3(1) (xii)
of SC/ST (PA) Act on the same set of evidence.

It is also so because if appellant was in a position to dominate the will of prosecutrix and he used that position to exploit the prosecutrix sexually for which she would not have otherwise agreed, then, in that case, consent given by the prosecutrix would not be a free consent.
Hence, offence under Section 376 of IPC shall also be made out.

Still,
learned trial Court has acquitted the appellant for the offence under Section NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30820 4 CRA-407-2004 376 of IPC but convicted the appellant under Section 3 (1) (xii) of SC/ST (PA) Act.
9. It is pertinent to note that respondent/State has not filed any appeal against the acquitted of the appellant for the offence under Section 376 of IPC.
Therefore, findings of trial Court with respect to aforesaid have attained finality.
Further, in the instant case, there is no caste certificate of competent authority on record.

Therefore, prosecutrix is not proved to be a member of Scheduled Ratan Lal vs The State Of M.P. on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16533505/
2 Caste.
10.

sentences.text: Hence, in view of discussion in the foregoing paras, learned trial Court has materially erred in convicting and sentencing the appellant for the offence under Section 3 (1) (xii) of SC/ST (PA) Act.
11. Resultantly, appeal filed by the appellant is allowed and impugned judgment passed by the trial Court is hereby set-aside and appellant is acquitted of aforesaid offences .

12. Let a copy of this order be sent forthwith to the concerned Trial Court for information and necessary action.
13.
